For this type of policy mapping, weighting variables are not applicable; the relevant “data preparation” is the compilation of governance information from OECD and partner sources.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD country note explains how Finland’s adult skills system is governed across national, regional, and local levels, emphasizing a combined education-and-skills structure rather than a separate adult-education system. It outlines responsibilities for VET, HVET, CET, and ALMPs, including which ministries and agencies set strategy, provide intelligence/implementation, and allocate funding, as well as how delivery is devolved to municipalities and other providers. The note also describes the role of regional councils and ELY Centres in long-term planning and skills-needs forecasting, and it highlights recent decentralisation of employment services to municipalities (from January 2025) through employment areas. Benchmarks are presented descriptively (e.g., subnational share of general government expenditure) rather than as statistical performance metrics. Because the document is not an empirical student-assessment analysis, it does not use ILSA-style scaling, plausible values, or ML-based predictive modeling.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is sparse by design because the provided text is a governance/policy country note, not an empirical study with an analytic sample, measurement model, or predictive modeling results. Consequently, fields such as total_students, country-level sample sizes, PV handling, missing-data handling, and ML techniques are not meaningfully defined in the manuscript body. The document’s purpose is descriptive synthesis of institutional roles and responsibilities across governance levels.
